description: Backend: finish the Job Scheduler pipeline (B3, B4, B6, B7, B8, B9, B10) and fix the updateSchedule validation bug so scheduleIntervalDays is restricted to the [1, 7, 30] presets everywhere, matching ALLOWED_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_DAYS in updateProfile.ts. Independent of FEAT-002 except that FEAT-002 depends on PUT /me/schedule already behaving correctly (fixed here).
steps: Create backend/src/serverless/resources/matches-table.ts exporting getMatchesTableResources(), modeled on jobs-table.ts: table 'job-scout-${sls:stage}-matches', PK/SK string attrs, GSI1 (gsi1pk, gsi1sk) with ProjectionType ALL, PAY_PER_REQUEST billing, Outputs.MatchesTableName export.

Wire the new table into backend/serverless.ts: import getMatchesTableResources, merge into Resources/Outputs next to cvBucketResources/jobsTableResources; add MATCHES_TABLE_NAME: { Ref: 'MatchesTable' } to provider.environment; add a provider.iam.role.statements entry granting dynamodb:GetItem/BatchGetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/Query on the MatchesTable ARN and its GSI1 index ARN; add bedrock:InvokeModel (Resource arn:aws:bedrock:${aws:region}::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0) and ses:SendEmail/ses:SendRawEmail (Resource '*' for MVP) statements; add SES_FROM_ADDRESS and BEDROCK_MODEL_ID to provider.environment (same ssm/env pattern as cognitoIssuerUrl).

Fix backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/updateSchedule/updateSchedule.ts: replace the MIN/MAX_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_DAYS range check with a local `ALLOWED_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_DAYS: readonly number[] = [1, 7, 30]` constant (duplicated from updateProfile.ts's convention, do not import across modules) and make validateScheduleIntervalDays reject anything not in that array, message 'scheduleIntervalDays must be 1, 7, or 30'. Also make the function write gsi1pk = `SCHED#${schedulerEnabled}` whenever schedulerEnabled changes, and gsi1sk = `NEXT#${nextRunAt}` whenever nextRunAt is written (the enable-with-no-prior-nextRunAt branch already computes nextRunAt; reuse it).

Update backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/updateSchedule/_tests/updateSchedule.test.ts: change the 'accepts integers from 1 to 30' test to assert only 1/7/30 are accepted and 0/14/31 are rejected; add assertions that gsi1pk/gsi1sk appear in the UpdateExpression/ExpressionAttributeValues on enable and on disable.

Add MatchResult type to backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/types.ts (partitionKey, userId, jobId, matchScore, reasoning, matchingSkills, sentAt?, evaluatedAt), verbatim from specs/02-database-schema.md §3.

Create backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/loadExistingMatches.ts: loadExistingMatchIds(userId, jobIds) using BatchGetCommand against MATCHES_TABLE_NAME with keys { PK: '${userId}#${jobId}', SK: 'MATCH' }, chunked at 100 keys per call, returning the Set of jobIds that already exist (ignore sentAt). Also export dedupeByJobId(jobs) for in-run deduplication.

Add backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/_tests/loadExistingMatches.test.ts mocking @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb the way upsertJobPosting's test does; cover matched-jobId detection, >100-key chunking into multiple BatchGetCommands, and dedupeByJobId.
Add @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime and @aws-sdk/client-ses to backend/package.json dependencies.

Create backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/evaluateJobs.ts: evaluateJobsForUser(userId, targetRoles, jobs, deps?) calling Bedrock anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0 with max_tokens 300 via InvokeModelCommand per job, parsing the JSON response into { matchScore, reasoning, matchingSkills } defensively (skip + log on parse failure, never throw), then PutItem a MatchResult row (PK `${userId}#${jobId}`, SK 'MATCH', gsi1pk `USER#${userId}`, gsi1sk `SCORE#${matchScore}#${jobId}`, evaluatedAt now, no sentAt). The Bedrock call must be an injectable dependency for tests, following the FetchHtml injection pattern in scrapeJobs.ts.

Add backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/_tests/evaluateJobs.test.ts covering a successful evaluation, a malformed-JSON response being skipped without throwing, and the PutCommand payload shape.

Create backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/sendDigest.ts: sendDigestForUser(userEmail, newMatches, jobsById, deps?) filtering newMatches to matchScore >= MATCH_SCORE_THRESHOLD (define = 60, documented inline as the MVP 'high-score' cutoff); if the filtered list is empty, return { sent: false } without calling SES at all; otherwise build one HTML digest body and send via SendEmailCommand from process.env.SES_FROM_ADDRESS, then UpdateItem each included match's row to set sentAt = now, returning { sent: true, matchIds }.

Add backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/_tests/sendDigest.test.ts covering: zero qualifying matches skips SendEmailCommand entirely, a qualifying match sends once and sets sentAt via UpdateCommand.

Create backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/advanceSchedule.ts: advanceUserSchedule(userId, scheduleIntervalDays) computing lastRunAt = now (UTC ISO) and nextRunAt = lastRunAt + scheduleIntervalDays * 86400000 ms, then UpdateCommand on UsersTable setting lastRunAt, nextRunAt, updatedAt, and gsi1sk = `NEXT#${nextRunAt}` (gsi1pk left as SCHED#true). Must run on every successful pipeline completion, even with zero new matches.
Add backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/_tests/advanceSchedule.test.ts asserting nextRunAt is exactly scheduleIntervalDays days after lastRunAt for 1/7/30, and gsi1sk is refreshed.

Create backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/runSchedulerPipelineForUser.ts orchestrating: runUserPipeline (B5, untouched) -> dedupeByJobId -> loadExistingMatchIds filter (B6) -> evaluateJobsForUser on the remainder (B7) -> sendDigestForUser with the new matches (B8) -> advanceUserSchedule always (B9). Every sub-step injectable as a dependency, same pattern as RunUserPipelineDeps.

Add backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/runUserPipeline/_tests/runSchedulerPipelineForUser.test.ts (this is the B10 verification): run the orchestrator twice for the same user/job, injecting a fake loadExistingMatchIds returning {} on run 1 and the job's jobId on run 2; assert evaluateJobsForUser and sendDigestForUser mocks are invoked with that job on run 1 and are NOT invoked with that jobId on run 2 — proving Bedrock/SES are never called again for an already-matched jobId.

Create backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/dispatcher/dispatcher.ts: dispatchDueUsers(deps?) running a QueryCommand on UsersTable GSI1 (KeyConditionExpression 'gsi1pk = :pk AND gsi1sk <= :sk', :pk = 'SCHED#true', :sk = 'NEXT#' + nowIso); for each due user, skip (log reason) if cvS3Key missing or targetRoles empty, else call runSchedulerPipelineForUser sequentially, catching and logging any per-user error so one failure doesn't stop the batch.

Create backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/dispatcher/handler.ts: a plain (non-middy, no API Gateway) Lambda entry calling dispatchDueUsers and logging a summary via the existing Logger/SCHEDULER_SERVICE pattern.

Register the new function in backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/index.ts as schedulerDispatcher: { handler: 'src/modules/schedulerModule/dispatcher/handler.main', timeout: 300, memorySize: 1024, events: [{ schedule: { rate: ['rate(1 hour)'] } }] } — IAM-triggered only, one shared tick, never per-user.

Add backend/src/modules/schedulerModule/dispatcher/_tests/dispatcher.test.ts covering: a due user with CV+roles is processed, a user missing cvS3Key is skipped, a user with empty targetRoles is skipped, and one user's thrown error doesn't prevent the next user from being processed.
acceptance_criteria: `cd backend && npx jest updateSchedule --config=jest.config.js` passes, including new tests proving only 1/7/30 are accepted and gsi1pk/gsi1sk are written.
`cd backend && npx jest loadExistingMatches evaluateJobs sendDigest advanceSchedule runSchedulerPipelineForUser dispatcher --config=jest.config.js` all pass.

The runSchedulerPipelineForUser test demonstrates a second run never calls the injected Bedrock-evaluation or SES-digest dependencies for a jobId that already has a MatchResult (B10 satisfied by an automated test, not a manual check).
`cd backend && npm test` (full suite, including the untouched B1/B2/B5 tests) passes.
`cd backend && npm run compile` reports no type errors.
`cd backend && npm run lint` reports zero warnings.
serverless.ts defines exactly one EventBridge schedule (rate(1 hour)) for schedulerDispatcher — no AWS::Events::Rule per user anywhere in the diff.
verification: cd backend && npx jest loadExistingMatches evaluateJobs sendDigest advanceSchedule runSchedulerPipelineForUser dispatcher --config=jest.config.js
findings: PUT /me/schedule now rejects any scheduleIntervalDays that isn't exactly 1, 7, or 30 (BadRequestError: 'scheduleIntervalDays must be 1, 7, or 30'), matching ALLOWED_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_DAYS in updateProfile.ts — the prior 1-30 range bug is fixed, so FEAT-002 should only ever offer the Daily(1)/Weekly(7)/Monthly(30) presets with no custom day input. The response shape of PUT /me/schedule (UserProfile, via withProfileDefaults) is unchanged — same fields as before (scheduleIntervalDays, schedulerEnabled, nextRunAt, etc.), just with the validation bug fixed and gsi1pk/gsi1sk now also written server-side (not exposed to the frontend). No API contract changes beyond the stricter validation message. Backend scheduler pipeline (B3/B4/B6-B10) is fully implemented and independent of the frontend; FEAT-002 has no new backend dependency beyond PUT /me/schedule behaving correctly, which is now verified by tests (14 passing updateSchedule tests + full backend suite of 149 tests, tsc --noEmit clean, eslint --max-warnings=0 clean).
